header.sector: AI accelerators, GPUs, custom silicon and their direct supply chain
header.title: GB300/GB200 vs AMD MI355X serving-cost leadership depends on latency constraints

s01_bottom_line.text: In SemiAnalysis's InferenceX GLM-5.3 serving benchmark, NVIDIA GB300/GB200 lead on modeled cost at 150 tokens/sec (GB200 ~12% cheaper than MI355X on total tokens), but AMD MI355X ATOM leads at 100 tps and, under a two-second TTFT limit, is about 9% cheaper than B200; GB300 becomes cheapest only when the TTFT limit is relaxed to ten seconds. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩

The article states that across the three streaming-speed targets neither system has a uniform cost advantage and that GB300's throughput lead is more than offset by its higher assumed hourly cost at the 150 tps target. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩

No vendor has a uniform cost advantage across streaming-speed targets and latency constraints, so competitive positioning between NVIDIA and AMD in inference serving is workload- and constraint-dependent rather than decisively won by one side.

items.text: GB200 is about 12% lower cost than MI355X ATOM at the 150 tokens/sec target. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
ATOM costs about 13% less than GB200 at 100 tokens/sec; GB200 costs about 5% less at 125 and 12% less at 150. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
Under a two-second TTFT limit, MI355X ATOM costs $0.0607 per million total tokens vs $0.0666 for B200, about 9% less.
With a ten-second TTFT limit, GB300 with Dynamo-TRT-LLM costs $0.0451, about 26% below ATOM's $0.0607. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
GB300 delivers the lowest modeled serving cost at 150 tokens per second response speed in SemiAnalysis's comparison.
At 150 tokens/sec, GB200 costs approximately $0.044 per million total tokens. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩

s03_transmission.text: GLM-5.3 agentic serving is benchmarked across NVIDIA GB300/GB200 and AMD MI355X using different inference engines and latency targets. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩

Modeled serving cost per million tokens shifts between vendors with the streaming-speed target and TTFT limit; GB200 ~12% cheaper at 150 tps, MI355X ~13% cheaper at 100 tps. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
